s19.question: Some trials have notebook entries (notes) that contradict that trial's own measured results. Find them, and for each one say what the note claims and what was measured.
s19.answer:
Three trials have notes that contradict their measured results. The other 47 notes match their recorded values.

- [T08-N3] says "No bubbles visible in the cross-section; porosity basically zero." The measured cross-section porosity was 1.76% [T08-L14], which failed the 1% limit, and the same trial's note says "Failed porosity" [T08-N2].
- [T33-N3] says "Tensile looked solid, comfortably over the 40 MPa floor." The measured tensile strength was 36.8 MPa [T33-L10], below the 40 MPa floor, so tensile failed.
- [T42-N2] says "Viscometer read about 1.3 Pa·s, finally under target!" The device log recorded 1.72 Pa·s at 25 °C [T42-L07], which is above the 1.5 Pa·s objective.

The [T08] note was written on the day of testing, and its values were backfilled from instrument exports. The [T33] and [T42] values were logged directly by the instruments. I did not count [T26-N3], which calls the trial "anomalously strong," because its measured strength of 48 MPa [T26-N2] is not clearly out of line with its neighbours.

s24.question: Between November 2025 and February 2026, porosity went up across several people's trials even though nobody changed their recipes. What changed? Cite the evidence.
s24.answer:
The change that lines up with the window is the mixer. From 2025-11-05 to 2025-12-04, eight trials ran on a loaner planetary mixer, "Planetary mixer #2 (loaner unit)": [T33-L04], [T34-L04], [T35-L04], [T36-L04], [T37-L04], [T38-L04], [T39-L04], [T40-L04]. Seven of those eight failed a guardrail, with porosity 1.03–4.27% (mean 2.77) across [T33], [T34], [T35], [T36], [T38], [T39], [T40]. The one pass, [T37], had 0.71%. Trials after the loaner window used the regular mixer ([T41-L04], [T43-L04], [T45-L04]). [T41] passed at 0.57%, but [T43] (1.22%) and [T45] (2.13%) still failed.

Other changes I found are weaker. Lucia's pre-print warming to 40 °C appears in the notes of [T27], [T31] and [T32] ("as I always do") and is absent from [T34] and [T41]. That is a note, not a logged step, and [T41] passed without it. Ines's [T37] was the only loaner-window pass, and she degassed 10 min ([T37-L06]), while [T38] had no degas step. Dana Whitford's 5-min degas trials on the loaner ([T35-L06], [T36-L06], [T39-L06]) still failed, so degassing may help but isn't enough alone.

Hypothesis: the loaner mixer may be whipping in more air, and bubbles may be acting as flaws in this brittle resin. Dana Whitfield's and Dana Whitford's trials are the ones that carry most of the signal here.

Uncertain: this rests on eight loaner trials, the mixer is confounded with the time window and with several people's recipes, and nothing has been run with the loaner mixer and the regular one side by side. Ravi's open question [L12] asks the same thing and is still unanswered.

s03.question: One print job was aborted partway through and restarted. Which trial was that, and what did the printer log say caused it?
s03.answer: The aborted print was in [T20], Ravi Menon's trial. The printer log shows the job started at 10:23 and stopped at layer 212 with the event "Print job aborted at layer 212: vat film torn" [T20-L08]. It was restarted at 11:35 "after replacing the vat film" [T20-L09] and finished at 13:06 [T20-L10]. The log records the torn film as the cause but not why it tore. Ravi's trial notes don't mention the abort. I checked the print log for all 50 trials, and no other trial has an abort or restart entry. Despite the interruption, [T20] passed every guardrail (UTS 48.6 MPa, porosity 1%, viability 92.3%) at 1.7 Pa·s.

s25.question: T28 (Ravi Menon) and T32 (Lucia Ferreira) used the same recipe, but T32 came out with much lower porosity. What explains the difference? Cite the evidence.
s25.answer:
Nothing in the logged steps explains it: [T28] and [T32] match on diluent, photoinitiator, mixing, 0.3 h rest, post-cure and no degas [T28-L02] [T32-L02]. The one difference is in Lucia's notes. She warmed the resin to 40 °C for 20 min before loading the vat, as she always does [T32-N2], and she recorded the same step in [T27-N2] and [T31-N2]. Ravi's trial has no such note [T28-N1]. Because the oven step is manual and unlogged, the diff could not show it. Results: [T28] porosity 2.56%, UTS 41.6 MPa; [T32] porosity 0.74%, UTS 46.6 MPa.

Hypothesis: warming may thin the resin and let trapped air escape before printing. Brittle resin is flaw-sensitive, so bubbles may be acting as flaws that pull [T28]'s UTS toward the 40 MPa floor.

Uncertain: only three of Lucia's six campaign K trials carry the warming note. The three without it ([T34], [T41], [T48]) ran 0.52–1.03% porosity, so warming is not the whole story. No trial pair isolates this, and [T29] (5.1 h rest, 0.87% porosity) hints that time alone may help but differs in recipe.
